data.title: CDN
data.tagline: Serve static files from locations closer to visitors
data.description: A content delivery network caches images, scripts, styles, and sometimes pages across many edge locations. It can reduce latency and protect the origin from repeated traffic. Plan cache rules and invalidation so visitors do not receive outdated files.

use: Cache public files with stable versions
Absorb repeated requests before they reach the origin
avoid: Cache private or personalized responses as public
Change a file without updating or invalidating its cache
Assume a CDN fixes slow application logic

lessonPractice.title: Product images load slowly overseas. After adding a CDN, some regions still show an old image after release. What is the complete response?

options.label: Serve static images through the CDN and use versioned URLs or purge before regional verification
options.feedback: The CDN shortens delivery for static assets, while versioning or purge prevents nodes from serving an old cache.

options.label: Keep the same image URL and extend its cache lifetime while waiting for every region to update naturally
options.feedback: A longer cache on the same URL preserves old copies for longer and provides no reliable update point.

options.label: Bypass the CDN after release and treat a fresh origin image as proof every region has updated
options.feedback: A fresh origin does not prove edge caches have refreshed; verify versions, cache state, and real regions.

data.agentPrompt: Serve images, JS, and CSS through the CDN with versioned filenames, then verify cache hits and multiple regions after release. Do not long-cache inventory or balances; measure CDN, origin, and backend time separately for slow APIs.
